prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Purpose: original buildable environment concept art for a premium survival game set in an abandoned, drowned subtropical coastal city several generations after people left. Invent solely from this written description. No photographs, no other game's imagery, no existing franchise designs.
Medium: polished digital PAINTING in stylized realism, high-end game art, confident designed forms, rich tactile materials, believable warm late-afternoon sunlight and cool sky fill in shadows. Handsome, restrained, specific. Not photoreal photography, not cartoon, not loose sketch.
Palm construction: every crown consists of distinct pinnate feather fronds with a visible midrib, many slim leaflets on both sides, a rising arch and drooping tip. Open wedges of sky between fronds; clear radial crown star. Never fan palms, banana leaves, fern blobs or fuzzy green balls. Individual trees vary in age, height, lean, crown fullness, missing fronds and minor scars. All crowns grow radially in 3D and work from every azimuth.
Royal: nearly straight smooth pale grey column, subtle swell below mid-height, taper toward a glossy bright green 1.5–2 m crownshaft, 3–4 m arching fronds, compact elevated crown; mature height 14–20 m, trunk about 0.5 m wide with 0.6 m swell. Coconut: slender grey-brown ringed trunk 9–14 m along its curve, 0.3–0.4 m wide, leaning outward then rising, occasional kink/S curve, broad loose 8–10 m crown of 4–5 m drooping fronds, coconuts and old flower stalks just under crown, 0–3 hanging dead brown fronds. Bases flare gently into very tight low mats of thin roots immediately around the trunk, never sprawling roots, buttresses or root stilts.
Output: one finished PNG, landscape canvas, maximum native resolution available; aim for 3840 x 2160. No watermark or decorative border.
Asset: coconut_lineup.png. Side elevation lineup of exactly FOUR complete coconut palms with entirely separate silhouettes. Each whole tree and every frond tip inside image; generous quiet space between trees. All stand at the same depth on a narrow strip of pale beach sand mixed with cracked old concrete. Quiet light warm sky, thin subdued turquoise horizon, no other trees or busy background. A single 1.8 m explorer stands upright by the second base, same depth as trees, accurately about one sixth of their height.
Left to right: C1 has a 13 m slender trunk following a long outward lean then a graceful upward recovery, medium full 19-frond crown and 9 green/yellow coconuts in two clusters. C2 a 10 m trunk with a pronounced angular healed kink low down then upright terminal section, sparse 13-frond crown with a clear missing sector and two dead brown fronds hanging down close to the upper trunk, several old branching flower stalks. C3 a 14 m trunk forming a shallow S with different bends through its height, broad full crown of 22 distinct arching/drooping fronds, 12 fruits in green/yellow/brown clusters, one dead hanging frond. C4 a 9 m shorter wind-shaped palm, strong oblique lean then lifted tip, 15-frond asymmetrical crown, no fruits and one straw-yellow low frond. Alternate projected lean directions so these read as independent life histories.
Trunk diameters 0.3–0.4 m, compact swollen base 0.6–0.8 m wide; dense low thin roots embedded just beside base, no raised spreading roots or buttresses. Clearly articulated compressed irregular rings, grey-brown fibrous weathering, occasional flattened impact scar; never a royal green crownshaft. Crowns 8–10 m across and fronds 4–5 m long, loose, countable midribs, leaflets hanging from BOTH sides. Sunlit fresh green upright center, deep green outer blades, some yellow lower fronds. Do not turn crown into a dense feathery ball. Small labels underneath ground only: "C1", "C2", "C3", "C4"; beside person "1.8 m".
